payload.detail: Earlier live desktop pass on psychiatry.tools prescribing mode: CrCl typed as 95 briefly displayed 42095; QTc showed unexpected 420. Suspected race in clinical-dashboard patient-profile NumberField (type=number + render sync) with writePatientProfile on every keystroke. 2026-09-13 re-verification could NOT reproduce (CrCl 95 and QTc 450 displayed correctly under slow type, replace, backspace). SaMD memo discusses broader patient-profile classification but does not evidence this corruption. Keep OPEN as a low-priority watch until Playwright digit-by-digit asserts values never gain foreign prefixes — do NOT treat as confirmed P1 clinical defect without reproduction. Stop: do not close from a single non-repro session alone; do not divert urgent clinical-safety work on suspicion alone. REPRODUCED AND FIXED 2026-09-18. No longer a watch item - the mechanism was found, reproduced in jsdom with digit-by-digit typing, and fixed. The field compared the incoming value against the previous prop and skipped the re-sync entirely while the current text was out of range, so a refused entry stayed on screen forever. Decisive failing assertions before the fix: expected '420' to be '95' (one mounted panel showing a CrCl the profile does not hold, while dosing alerts run on the other value) and expected '1' to be '1.0'. THE SECOND ONE IS WORSE AND WAS NOT PREVIOUSLY KNOWN: the sync re-derived the text from the stored number, so an in-progress '1.0' serum creatinine was rewritten to '1' under the caret and the next keystroke landed as 12 - and 12 mg/dL is in range, so it stored with no warning at all. An order-of-magnitude dosing input error, entered silently by a clinician who typed 1.02. THE FIX compares the incoming value against what the field last committed rather than against the previous prop, which separates the field's own write echoing through the shared store from news arriving elsewhere; an echo leaves the draft alone, news is adopted even over an out-of-range draft. Bounds, persistence and the error text are unchanged, and out-of-range text is still held for correction in place. Six new DOM cases cover CrCl, QTc, the multi-mount desync, the decimal path and a leading zero; three of them fail without the fix. REMAINDER RAISED SEPARATELY: a refused entry still survives a clear performed from another mounted panel (drafted fix held back because it changes when inputs remount), and the single-mount case of typing into a box that visibly still has text, which is a design decision rather than a defect. The standing clinical question - what a number field should do with a partial entry - is the PATIENT-NUMERIC-FIELD-DISPLAY open assurance decision in docs/clinical-hazard-controls.json.
